Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Horsell, Surrey, 1894, oil lamp, black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:03. The shot opens on a medium close shot on the narrator's <Subject 2>, a slim straight-backed woman of twenty-nine with an oval face, wide hazel eyes and light freckles across the nose, her thick chestnut-auburn hair swept up into a soft pompadour, in a lilac-grey cotton house dress with a high collar and a white bibbed apron tied at the waist, a plain gold band on her hand at the table at night, her face deadly white in the lamplight, her brows knitted and her hand laid flat on the cloth halfway across it toward him, listening with her plate square in front of her. The camera is across the table level with her face, three paces from her, a 50mm lens. The oil lamp lights her from below. At the first frame the wife's head and shoulders fill the CENTRE of the frame, the panel cutting her at the middle of the chest. The shot is inside this place: the narrator's dining room at night in 1894: a small square room with a papered wall and a framed landscape print, a mahogany table laid with a white cloth, a cold joint and bread and a decanter of wine set out on it, two chairs drawn up, a sideboard against the wall and a curtained sash window. The camera tilts up from the cloth to her face, travelling a hand's breadth, until her eyes are in the middle of the picture as her hand goes on further across the cloth toward his, from 00:00 to 00:02. <Subject 1> (S1), on screen, oval face, with a clipped English voice at an even pace, says: <d>[English] They may come here.</d> Her mouth shapes every syllable as the line is heard and closes on the last word. At 00:02, as the line ends, the lamplight goes on moving on her face as the flame works, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:03 the camera is tilting up through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
